sentences.text: Parvinatator is an extinct genus of small marine reptile belonging to the group ichthyopterygians.
This animal is estimated to have been less than one meter in length.
The preserved skull fossil measures approximately 15 centimeters in width and 10 centimeters in height.
In the preserved left forefin, the ulna is reduced in length and width and is smaller than the radius.
Reconstruction of the eye socket suggests the creature had large eyes typical of ichthyosaurs, indicating it may have hunted in dark or deep water.
The forefin was likely used for controlling pitch rather than for locomotion.
The species Parvinatator wapitiensis was discovered in 1995 by Elisabeth Nicholls and Don Brinkman in the Sulfur Mountain Formation.
The genus Parvinatator was named by Nicholls and Brinkman in 1995.
Parvinatator is a genus represented by a single species, P. wapitiensis, which lived in the Early Triassic in what is now Canada.
Parvinatator likely fed on small fish and cephalopods based on its jaw size and tooth shape.
Parvinatator is classified within the family Parvinatatoridae.
Some researchers classify Parvinatator as a true ichthyosaur that is more derived than Utatsusaurus and Grippia.
Fossils of Parvinatator have been found in British Columbia, Canada.
Parvinatator lived approximately 251 to 235 million years ago during the Olenekian to Ladinian stages.
There is scientific disagreement regarding the exact phylogenetic position of Parvinatator among its relatives.
